newsitem.title: JORDAN: AMMAN SHARES EASE DESPITE CEMENT, PHARMACEUTICALS.
newsitem.headline: AMMAN SHARES EASE DESPITE CEMENT, PHARMACEUTICALS.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell slightly on Wednesday despite strong demand for pharmaceutical and cement stocks, brokers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.10 percent to 165.61 points in turnover worth 707,000 dinars ($1 million).

Pharmaceutical company Dar al-Dawa stocks rose 0.05 dinars to 5.35 dinars in turnover of 284,000 dinars. Jordan Cement Factory shares also gained in busy turnover and Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturers also gained 0.05 dinars to 4.11 dinars.
"There is high foreign demand for the pharmaceuticals and the cement firms," said Mohammad Abdallah, senior analyst at Pearl Consulting.
But the blue-chip gains were outnumbered by falling stock. Overall 11 shares rose and 15 fell, with another 18 trading but closing unchanged.
Stocks in companies which were boosted on Tuesday by hopes of better trade with Iraq under the second phase of the U.N.'s "oil-for-food" deal were quiet on Wednesday.
Jordan Selpho Chemicals closed unchanged at 0.63 dinars while Intermediate Petrochemicals slipped fractionally to 0.56 dinars from 0.57 dinars.

But shares in Irbid Electricity, Jordan's second largest electricity distribution firm, rose by the maximum daily five percent limit after officials announced they were looking for investors to link up with a local partner to buy up 51 percent of the company.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, fell 0.14 percent to 80.57 points, 3.54 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
